title: Marketplace tenant isolation readiness and asset brief
body:
Objective:
This brief outlines the operator-facing readiness checklist and the marketing asset requirements for partners listing Redwood Inference in cloud marketplaces when the offer involves tenant-isolated (VPC/private) deployments. Goal is to reduce back-and-forth during partner onboarding, surface security gating early, and provide copy snippets and acceptance criteria for listing teams and partner engineers.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: partner onboarding engineers, partner success managers, marketplace ops, legal review and listing copy owner.
- Scope: Marketplace tiles and catalog assets for offerings that require tenant isolation, private control plane, or bring-your-own-network (BYON). Not for pure-hosted API-only listings.

Quick summary of required approvals before submission:
1) Security signoff (SRE/Security): KMS/HSM pattern and data residency statement validated.
2) Network signoff (Infra): VPC peering/VPN patterns documented with sample topology.
3) Legal & Compliance: Data processing addendum and required contract clauses acknowledged.
4) Marketplace ops: Tile copy, SKU mapping, and trial entitlements validated.

Operator readiness checklist (detailed) - must be completed by partner eng + RI eng contact prior to marketplace submission:
- Identity & access:
  - Confirm SSO/IdP integration pattern (SAML/OIDC) and sample metadata file provided.
  - Explicit roles and least-privilege mapping documented (operator, auditor, app-admin).
  - Default credentials removal & ephemeral token rotation documented.

- Network and tenancy:
  - Provide one-page network topology: which subnets, NAT/GW, route tables, and expected egress IP ranges.
  - VPC peering or VPN configuration checklist with example handshake commands.
  - If using private control-plane, confirm accepted CIDR ranges and cross-account IAM roles.
  - Multi-tenant vs tenant-isolated: clearly call out which resources are per-tenant and which are shared.

- Data protection and keys:
  - KMS integration pattern and key rotation cadence documented. If partner uses their own KMS, list supported providers and permissions required.
  - At-rest encryption details, encryption algorithms, and where ephemeral caches (KV / prefix caches) are persisted.
  - Audit log retention and access controls (who can read logs, where stored).

- Compliance & residency:
  - Data residency statement: allowed regions, whether logs/metrics leave customer region, and any retained PII policy.
  - List of certifications relevant to the partner (SOC2, ISO27001, HIPAA) and outstanding gaps.

- Operational readiness:
  - SLA targets for the dedicated/private offering plus expected support hours/response times on marketplace listing.
  - Runbook snippets for common incidents: network flap, KMS outage, model fallback behavior.
  - Verification tests: smoke script that validates that a tenant can create a Workspace, call inference, and delete keys. Provide sample curl commands.

- Billing & provisioning:
  - SKU mapping for marketplace (trial SKU vs paid SKU). Include billing metering dimensions: per-token, per-inference-hour, or reserved capacity.
  - Trial provisioning gating: what entitlements are required to provision a tenant in private environment.

Acceptance criteria for marketplace tile and catalog assets:
- Technical artifacts must include: network topology PDF, KMS permissions dump, sample IdP metadata, sample smoke-test script, and support contact email alias.
- Copy must contain an explicit note on tenant isolation: short, clear sentence that explains what "tenant-isolated" means in the context of this listing.
- Tile must not assert certifications the partner or offering does not have. Any certification claims must be backed by artifact links.
- Pricing snippet must include a clear line item describing additional operational fees for private deployments (if any).

Sample short tile copy (3 variants) - use these as starting points for listing team edits:
1) "Redwood Inference — Private Tenant Edition: High-performance LLM inference with tenant-isolated deployments, certified control-plane options, and enterprise-grade key management for regulated workloads."
2) "Run production LLMs in your VPC: Redwood's tenant-isolated inference delivers predictable latency, KMS-backed encryption, and support for region-restricted data residency."
3) "Dedicated inference, private control plane: Bring secure, auditable LLM serving to regulated apps with flexible deployment and SLA-backed throughput."

Operator-facing asset checklist for marketplace ops (what to upload):
- Tile title, 1-line tagline, 2-3 bullet differentiators, long description (250-500 words).
- Network topology PDF (one page) labeled with partner and RI contact.
- Security artifact zip (KMS details, key policy snippets, audit log retention).
- IdP metadata XML (or sample) and instructions.
- Support & escalation contact info and hours.
- Pricing CSV with SKU mapping, trial entitlement details, and metering dimensions.

UX notes and copy constraints (things listing team should avoid):
- Avoid making claims like "FIPS-certified" unless documentation exists.
- Don’t use marketing-only phrases that obscure responsibilities (e.g., "fully managed by Redwood" when partner operates control plane). Instead use precise language.
- If the offering requires partner infra (BYON), add a clear callout in the tile: "Requires partner-managed VPC".

Unresolved questions / items to follow up (notes to self):
- Does marketplace demand a standardized trial uptime SLA for private offerings? Action: ask marketplace ops (JIRA-4567).
- How to represent per-region pricing on tiles when partner has variable infra costs? Action: catalog pricing workshop w/ finance.
- Should we include a short video walkthrough for tenant provisioning? Potentially helpful, ask partner success.

Smoke-test examples (operator shareable snippets):
- Create workspace (curl example, placeholder endpoint)
  curl -X POST https://example.redwood.internal/workspaces -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"name":"test-tenant"}'
- Run inference test:
  curl -X POST https://example.redwood.internal/infer -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"model":"gpt-small","input":"hello"}'
- Validate key access:
  aws kms describe-key --key-id <key-arn> --profile customer-account

Owner and handoffs:
- Primary owner: Asha Patel (go-to-market) - copy & tile coordination.
- Technical owner: Daniel Kim (solutions engineering) - all infra and network artifacts.
- Security reviewer: Priya Rao (security) - artifact signoff.

Timeline suggestion for a typical partner onboarding for tenant-isolated marketplace listing:
- Week 0: Intake and initial scoping call. Collect IdP and topology.
- Week 1: Engineering artifacts collected and smoke test run.
- Week 2: Security and legal reviews. Iterate copy.
- Week 3: Marketplace ops upload and listing QA.

Appendix: checklist quick table (copy for a checklist card) - (one-line items for quick triage):
- IdP metadata provided
- Network topology uploaded
- KMS pattern documented
- Sample smoke-tests pass
- Pricing CSV uploaded
- Support alias confirmed
- Compliance artifacts attached

Notes/voice: keep tile language precise and operator-friendly. This doc is a working template — expect tweaks per partner.

References / links in process: see linked_artifacts.

Last notes: prioritize making the marketplace tile reduce support load after launch — include clear gating artifacts so ops don't get left chasing infra details post-publish.

End of brief.
